proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-relative-external-power-regrouping] with $r=2$, $(X_1,K_1)=(P,K)$ and $(X_2,K_2)=(Q,L)$. Its $P_2$ is $W$, its $a_1,b_1$ are $a,b$, its $h_2$ is $h$, and its $T_2$ is exactly $H$. It gives that $P,W$ and these morphisms have the asserted geometric properties, and that $H\in D^b_{ctf}(W,A)$. Applying the same statement with $r=1$ and $(X_1,K_1)=(Q,L)$ gives that $Q$ is separated of finite type over $k$. Thus every scheme and morphism used below lies in its required finite-type field-base domain.

source.place: Relative-product steps (1),(3): geometric and coefficient domains

proof.text: The inputs $K$ and $H$ are bounded constructible: this is part of membership in $D^b_{ctf}$. Clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] gives bounded constructible etale representatives and comparison isomorphisms for both. These are witnesses in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Fix any witnesses $(K_0,e_K)$ and $(H_0,e_H)$; all subsequent assertions are on the bounded-below etale-origin domain, rather than on an exceptional-adjoint domain.

Apply [thm-sf-comp-composition] to $b:W\to Q$, $g:Q\to B$ and the chosen witness of $H$. Step 1 checks its separated finite-type morphism and finite-type scheme hypotheses. It says that $Rb_!$ preserves the bounded-below etale-origin class, so the iterated expression is defined, and gives its component $\alpha_{g,b,H}:Rg_!Rb_!H\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gb)_!H=Rh_!H$. It is a natural isomorphism for any witness and is independent of compactifications under its canonical comparisons.

By the nonemptiness assertion of [prop-compactification-refinement], applied to $f:P\to B$ between the finite-type $k$-schemes of Step 1, choose a compactification $c=(j,p)$ to compute $Rf_!$ in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and its base change $c'=(j',p')$ of [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Thus $p,p'$ are proper. By [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] they are separated and quasi-compact; [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] makes them quasi-separated. Degreewise etale extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], so $j_!K_0$ is bounded below (use a bounded-below representative of $K_0$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] to the proper square with vertical arrows $p,p'$ and input $j_!K_0$. Its specified comparison equality identifies the actual ambient ringed proper exchange in [def-exchange-projection] with the etale proper exchange after conjugation by the canonical pullback and counit-mate direct-image comparisons. This checks the proper factor, including its normalization; an arbitrary isomorphism between the endpoints would not suffice.

source.place: Etale-origin comparison of the proper factor

proof.text:
For the upper open square $(j,j',a, ar g')$, apply [lem-fix-site-open-exchange] to $K_0$. Its hypotheses require only open immersions, a Cartesian square, a finite commutative coefficient ring and a bounded-below input; all hold here, with finiteness of $A_{E,n}$ stated in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Its displayed equality identifies the canonical pro-etale open-base-change factor with the etale one under the specified open-extension and pullback comparisons. Now substitute this equality and Step 4's proper-factor equality into the two-arrow formula of [def-exchange-projection]. Write $C_s$ and $C_t$ for the source and target comparisons built from these proper/open and pullback comparisons. Substitution cancels the comparison at the intermediate object with its inverse and gives $\operatorname{Ex}^{c,p}_!(
u_P^*K_0)C_s=C_t
u_Q^*(\operatorname{Ex}^{c,e}_!(K_0))$. Here the two $\operatorname{Ex}^{c,e}_!$ factors are exactly the proper exchange and $Rp'_*( eta)$ of [def-cbc-exchange-map]. This is the required transport identity. Naturality of the two composites then conjugates their equal maps by $e_K:
u_P^*K_0\cong K$, proving the same identification for the chosen witness of $K$.

proof.text: Apply [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] with $X=P$, $Y=B$, $Y'=Q$, $X'=W$, $g'=a$, $f'=b$, coefficient ring $A$ and witness $(K_0,e_K)$. Use its supplied-compactification alternative with the $c$ already chosen; no additional qcqs hypothesis is needed. The theorem makes the transported exchange invertible and independent of both the witness and compactification under the transported canonical comparisons. Step 5 identifies that very transported arrow with the concrete $\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}$ of the statement. Consequently the concrete exchange has all these properties. The theorem applies to every bounded-below witness, so the initial arbitrary choices impose no additional condition.

proof.text: Finally let $E=\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}$ and $J=E^{-1}\otimes1_L$. Tensoring the inverse identities for $E$ with $1_L$ shows that $J^{-1}=E\otimes1_L$. The compactification formula [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] is a functor on the ambient derived category, hence $Rg_!(J)$ has inverse $Rg_!(J^{-1})$: apply the functor to the two inverse identities. These are exactly the displayed $Rg_!(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}^{-1}\otimes1_L)$ and its inverse. Step 3 likewise gives $\alpha_{g,b,H}^{-1}$ with inverse $\alpha_{g,b,H}$. All maps used are compact-support, pullback, tensor or comparison maps; the argument invokes no exceptional adjunction or duality assertion.

title: Etale-origin composition and exchange factors for a relative product
statement:
Use the concrete finite-coefficient operations of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $f:P\to B$ and $g:Q\to B$ be separated finite-type morphisms, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(P,A)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Q,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $W=P\times_BQ$ have projections $a:W\to P$, $b:W\to Q$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and put $h=fa=gb$ and $H=La^*K\otimes_A^L Lb^*L$. The schemes $P,Q,W$ are separated of finite type over $k$, and $a,b,h$ are separated of finite type. The complexes $K$ and $H$ are bounded constructible and admit étale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. For any such witnesses, the compact-support composition component of [thm-sf-comp-composition]
$$\alpha_{g,b,H}:Rg_!Rb_!H\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_!H$$
is defined and invertible. The component of the concrete compact-support exchange of [def-exchange-projection] for the Cartesian square $(a,b,f,g)$,
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}:Lg^*Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rb_!La^*K,$$
is the compactification exchange of [def-cbc-exchange-map] transported from the small étale site through the witness of $K$, and is an isomorphism independent of that witness and of compactification under the canonical comparisons. In particular, $Rg_!(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}^{-1}\otimes1_L)$ and $\alpha_{g,b,H}^{-1}$ are defined isomorphisms. These assertions concern the composition and exchange factors only, on the concrete étale-origin finite-coefficient domains; they assume no Verdier-duality axiom or unrestricted ambient pro-étale exceptional adjoint.
